subject: Service regression briefing + QBR asks
messages:
From: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@bluesky.media>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Embedded API regression — throughput drop and SLA impact

Avery —

We ran into a regression starting ~08:50 PDT this morning that affected our embedding throughput against the dedicated instance (customer-id: BSM-47). Latency and per-request token counts spiked; observed 4.2s median per-embedding vs our expected 0.45s, and we experienced a sustained 25% failure rate for ~35 minutes. This triggered our own monitoring alerts and caused a downstream batch job to back up.

We escalated on our side and confirmed the issue reproduced from multiple regions. Can you confirm receipt and any immediate mitigation you can apply? BlueSky needs a concise write-up for their leadership and a QBR slide that explains impact, root cause (if known), and next steps.

Relevant details we captured:
- Region: us-west1
- Model: redwood-v1-embed-large (pinned)
- First anomaly at 08:50 PDT; full recovery visible ~09:25 PDT
- Jobs impacted: nightly indexing job, live search index refresh

Attaching the BlueSky traces we captured. Please advise next steps and who on your side will provide an exec summary.

Thanks,
Jordan Hsu
Operations Manager, BlueSky Media
(attachment: blue_sky_incident_report_v1.pdf)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Hsu <jordan.hsu@bluesky.media>, Maria Chen <maria.chen@bluesky.media>
Date: 2026-09-20T11:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embedded API regression — throughput drop and SLA impact

Thanks Jordan — we received this and have been triaging. Quick internal note and immediate mitigations taken: 

- Timeline (internal):
  - 08:52 PDT: alert surfaced to on-call (Marissa)
  - 08:55 PDT: automatic fallback to smaller-quantized model for new requests (reduced latency but increased token cost)
  - 09:15 PDT: KV-cache hotkeys purged and prefix caches warmed; error rate dropped to <1%
  - 09:25 PDT: steady-state observed

- Initial hypothesis: a combination of KV-cache eviction storm + a recent kernel/patch roll flagged in the serving pool for that tenant. We are treating as a regression tied to cache invalidation plus suboptimal kernel fallback for long sequences.

Action plan (short):
- Marissa to lead a root-cause micro-postmortem and produce a 1-page exec summary for BlueSky (due EOD tomorrow). (attachment: kv-cache-trace.html)
- Jonas to run a capacity-sweep on the dedicated pool and confirm if any scheduled maintenance overlapped with the window (due 09/21 12:00 PDT).
- I will prepare the QBR slide skeleton and coordinate credits/contract impact with finance (need estimate from Marissa on tokens/cost delta).

Jordan/Maria — we will send a compact exec summary and a proposed credit/mitigation by EOD 09/21. Apologies for the disruption — we understand the downstream impact and are prioritizing communication and fixes.

Avery Johnson
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
(attachment: qbr-appendix-slides.pptx)

Date: 2026-09-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Root cause summary and action items (BSM-47 regression)

Avery / team —

Quick root-cause note after the micro-postmortem and log correlation: 
- Primary cause: an uncoordinated cache invalidation event triggered by a config roll that accidentally flipped a TTL param for prefix caching. That led to a short-lived surge of cold-KV cache misses.
- Secondary contributor: an internal kernel selection change we pushed to a subset of hosts last week that degrades fallback latency when the embedding sequence length exceeds 1.5x median — this surfaced under the cache-miss surge.

Impact quantification (measured):
- Window: 08:50 — 09:25 PDT
- Median latency: regressed to 4.2s (vs SLA target 0.5s)
- Errors: 25% transient failures (client retries mitigated ~09:10 onward)
- Workload cost delta for BlueSky during window: estimated +$1,850 (tokens + fallback model overhead)

Action items (owners & deadlines):
1) Remediate cache TTL misconfiguration and add guardrails to config-roll path (owner: Marissa Cole) — complete by 2026-09-24 EOD
2) Revert the kernel-selection change on the 10% canary hosts pending further perf tests (owner: Jonas Weber) — revert in next 4 hours and validate; full verification by 2026-09-22 12:00 PDT
3) Add a transient error-mitigation policy that auto-fails over to a warm-quantized variant after X retries (owner: Avery Johnson) — design doc by 2026-09-27
4) Finance & Sales to propose a goodwill credit (estimated range provided) and include a short contract addendum for SLA language (owner: Vivek Kulkarni for approval) — proposal by 2026-09-22 EOB

Deliverables:
- 1-page exec summary for BlueSky (Marissa) — due EOD 2026-09-21 (sent as draft to Jordan)
- QBR slide (Avery) — initial skeleton sent; need final language and credit numbers

I have attached the KV cache timeline and traces (kv-cache-trace.html) used in the analysis. Sending draft exec summary now for internal review.

— Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
